t: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
In one study on sleep and memory, volunteers learned a list of word pairs in the evening.
Half of them then slept normally, and half stayed awake through the night in the lab.
What the volunteers didn't know was that they would be tested again on the same word pairs the next morning.
They thought the study was about mood.
The group that slept remembered noticeably more pairs.
Interestingly, the difference was largest for pairs the volunteers had found difficult.
The researchers concluded that sleep may help strengthen new memories, especially weak ones.
They were careful to say that the study doesn't tell us exactly how much sleep is needed.
That's a question for future research.
